proposals.evidence: The legacy-font j in this survey represents printed ǰ, as verified visually in its Hindko and Gujari appendices; ssnp conversion currently turns it into y. The analysis follows the original affricate, preserves the current spelling, and does not posit a y-to-j sound change. The exact root columns were checked in the scan. Section 1 jáṭā gives Lahnda jaṛṛ, Punjabi jaṛ/jaṛh and Hindi/Marwari jaṛ “root”; the short-vowel survey form fits this branch, not section 3 *jāṭā. Turner’s discussion of possible Dravidian/Munda prehistory remains unresolved by this family link.

proposals.evidence: The legacy-font j in this survey represents printed ǰ, as verified visually in its Hindko and Gujari appendices; ssnp conversion currently turns it into y. The analysis follows the original affricate, preserves the current spelling, and does not posit a y-to-j sound change. CDIAL explicitly lists Lahnda/Awankari/Punjabi sajjā “righthand” and Sindhi sāj̄o in sajya, distinguishing this family from savya “left”. Masculine/feminine and agreement variants, including both members of the selected slash responses, share the same stem. Gujari printed soǰi/soǰo and sajjo/sajji were checked; their vowel and gemination notation is retained.

proposals.evidence: The legacy-font j in this survey represents printed ǰ, as verified visually in its Hindko and Gujari appendices; ssnp conversion currently turns it into y. The analysis follows the original affricate, preserves the current spelling, and does not posit a y-to-j sound change. Full jána explicitly gives Lahnda jaṇā “person, husband”, Awankari jaṇā “person”, Sindhi j̄aṇo and Marwari jaṇo. This directly supports both survey senses and the local n/ṇ and final-vowel variants. Responses mixing this stem with ādmī, bandā or xasam are excluded; both alternatives in yano / yaṇā are accounted for.
